english: you put your foot in your mouth
also: if only you had kept quiet

terms.comment: Literally “oh, if you had kept quiet, you would have remained a philosopher”. Made from a story in Boethius (Cōnsōlātiō philosophiae 2, prose 7): a man who boasts of being a philosopher is told that he would have been taken for one had he kept quiet. We have read that passage only in translation, and have not found the saying in this form in an ancient text.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Boethius, Consolatio philosophiae 2, prose 7, read in the Project Gutenberg translation (12 November 2026).
